To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following is a sufficient and necessary (i.e., necessary and sufficient) condition for the consistency of a DTD D: for every non-empty set S of elements in D, the DTD D contains an XML document conforming to S.
a DTD is consistent if and only if the set of XML documents that are conformant to the DTD is not empty.
a DTD is consistent if and only if it is possible to construct an XML document that conforms to the structure imposed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions: (i) What is the consistency of DDTDs? (ii) How to determine whether a DTD is consistent or not?

the following issues: - What is the notion of the validity of an XML DTD? - What are the sufficient and necessary conditions for a DTD being valid? - How to construct an algorithm to test the validity of a given DTD?

the following questions: (1) What are the necessary conditions for the consistency of a DTD? (2) What are the sufficient conditions for the consistency? (3) How can we verify whether a DTD is consistent or inconsistent?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a DTD is consistent if and only if the corresponding graph is a forest.
the consistency of a DTD is equivalent to the consistency of its associated finite state automaton.
a DTD is consistent if and only if the set of all possible XML documents conforming the DTD is a regular language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a DTD is consistent if and only if it is possible to assign a unique label for each of its elements and attributes.
we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for a DDTD to be consistent.
we have developed a method for checking whether or not a given DTD is consistent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consistency of DXTs can be checked by checking the consistency of the corresponding DTDs, which can be done in linear time with respect to the size of the DTD.
a DTD is consistent if and only if the DTD is free of cycles in its containment hierarchy.
the consistency of DDTDs can be decided in polynomial time, which is a major step toward the development of automated techniques for the verification of XML DTD consistency.
